title: Pipkin and the Shy Moon Smile
markdown:
The twilight painted the sky soft purple and pale pink. Toby the bridge maker, Pipkin the hamster, and Auntie Flo were nestled on their softest blanket for a moon picnic. A gentle breeze carried the sweet scent of jasmine.

“Look, Toby!” squeaked Pipkin. “The moon looks like a tiny smile tonight! Yesterday it was a whole round cookie!” A little worry fluttered in his heart.

Toby smoothed the blanket. “It does look different, doesn’t it?” he murmured.

Auntie Flo, on a low branch, blinked her wise golden eyes. “My little Pipkin,” she hooted softly. “The moon is always a lovely round ball. It’s the sun’s light that makes it look different.”

Pipkin tilted his head. “But… it looks like a sliver!”

Auntie Flo chuckled. “Imagine this apple is the moon, and this pebble is like our sun.” She held the pebble low, letting its glow fall on just one side of the apple. “When we look from here,” she said, “we only see a little sliver of the apple’s sunny side. That’s what you see tonight—like a shy smile peeking out.”

Toby made a little platform of moss and stones so Pipkin could see better.

Auntie Flo moved the pebble slowly. As she turned the apple, more of its sunny side was revealed. Soon the whole apple looked like a bright circle. “This,” Auntie Flo whispered, “is our full moon, like a giant face watching over us.”

Pipkin gasped, his hamster eyes wide. “Oh! It is always round! We just see different parts of its sunshine!” Relief washed over him, warm as moonlight.

“Exactly,” Auntie Flo hooted. “The moon is always a round friend, but how much of its shining face we see depends on where the sun is pointing its light. We call these different views the phases of the moon. It’s a lovely slow dance.”

Toby smiled. “It’s like building a bridge to see something new,” he said.

Pipkin snuggled close to Toby, feeling safe and happy. He knew that even when the moon looked like a shy smile, its happy round face was always there. As the stars began to twinkle, Pipkin yawned a tiny sleepy yawn, feeling wonderfully peaceful. Soon he, Toby, and Auntie Flo would be tucked into their cozy beds, dreaming sweet dreams of the always-round moon. And Pipkin couldn’t wait to discover what other wonderful secrets were waiting in the moonlight.
characters: Toby (a moss-platform bridge maker), Pipkin (a picnic hamster), Flo (a golden-eyed picnic owl)
